title: Quiet-window promoter with telemetry-lock and resumable rollback
author: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Recent staged promotions showed noisy spikes from background traffic (batch retries and health checks) that contaminated canary signal windows. Small canaries would pass locally but later regress in production because our observation windows were polluted and rollback playbooks were brittle.

Goal: introduce a 'quiet-window' promotion primitive that temporarily mutes low-value noise traffic and pins a telemetry baseline (telemetry-lock) for the duration of a canary sampling window, combined with resumable rollback snapshots so a promotion can be reverted deterministically if signals cross thresholds. Deliver a developer-facing config + runtime enforcement inside the rollout controller.

What this PR does (single-contiguous description): Adds a QuietWindow step to the rollout graph and a telemetry-lock mechanism that freezes baseline aggregations for selected metrics for the sampling window; implements a lightweight traffic-labeling injector to mark noise sources (healthchecks, batch-retries, internal probes) and gate them out of canary cohorts; captures a resumable rollback snapshot that includes routing map + KV snapshot of model version metadata so reversion is instant and idempotent. Includes end-to-end tests in the rollout-sim harness and a canary smoke job that validates both forward promote and resume rollback paths.

Checklist: - [x] rollout-controller: add QuietWindow node type and graph semantics - [x] telemetry: telemetry-lock implementation + baseline snapshot API - [x] ingress: traffic-label injector and noise-policy config - [x] resume-rollback: snapshot creation and apply path with idempotency checks - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs: rollout reference and operator playbook - [x] e2e smoke in perf lab

Impact: Enables more deterministic canary assessments by reducing signal contamination and reducing human intervention during reverts. The snapshot-based rollback reduces mean-time-to-recover for bad promotes from minutes (manual) to < 30s in most test scenarios.

Backward compatibility: All new behavior is opt-in via rollout spec fields (quietWindow, noiseLabels, telemetryLock). Default rollout behavior unchanged.

Notes and rationale: We experimented with adaptive filtering inside metrics ingestion but found it brittle across tenants; pushing noise-labeling to the edge (ingress) with a small policy language keeps semantics explicit and auditable. Telemetry-lock stores a short-lived baseline vector and a hash so rollouts compare live windows to the locked baseline (instead of re-computing a moving baseline that drifts during a promote). Resume rollback takes a snapshot of the model routing map and the KV cache pointers to avoid cache-warmup inconsistencies on revert.

Tests & validation: Added 12 unit tests, 3 integration tests, and an e2e smoke job that runs in the benchmark-lab environment. Benchmarks in perf lab show quiet-window has negligible CPU overhead (<2%) and reduces false-positive canary alerts by ~78% in our synthetic noisy workload.

Migration/playbook (SUMMARY): 1) Append quietWindow block in rollout spec, optionally set noiseLabels to known probes. 2) Start small (1% traffic), monitor telemetry-lock stability. 3) If rollback trigger fires, operator can run `rw rollout resume-rollback <id>` which uses stored snapshot to revert routing map and KV pointers. 4) If issues persist, follow documented operator playbook to escalate (linked in PR docs).

Related: ENG-2345 (design doc), PM-4120 (product acceptance criteria), SUP-87 (support case that motivated this).
